top_choice_rationale: P001 credits a concrete, independently reproduced invention: the magic-wavelength optical lattice that cancels the light shift so many atoms are interrogated at once, taking clocks from the 1e-15 range to about 1e-18, confirmed by intercomparisons in several countries. The two-name allocation (Katori, Ye) is the cleanest on the table and has the broadest support. The citation must stay tied to the invention and its demonstrated accuracy, not to a redefinition of the second. P002 is mature and robust but its three-name credit leaves out Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (deceased) and the 3D work, and it sits close to the 2016 topology prize. It ranks second, clearly above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; atomic clocks and topological insulators are outside my expertise and I have no tie to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp
